title: The Optative Mood
objectives: Understand optative uses (wish, potential, indirect speech)
Use the optative in conditional sentences

vocabulary.definition: if (with optative in less vivid conditions)

grammar.explanation: The optative expresses wish, potentiality, or softened assertion. It uses the mood suffix -ι- or -ιη-/-οι-. Less common in Koine than in Classical Greek, it still appears in wishes, potential statements, and after secondary sequence verbs.

paradigms.name: Optative Uses
rows: if he should loose, he would be happy

rules: No augment in any optative form
Less common in Koine; sometimes replaced by subjunctive

exercises.question: Translate: μὴ γένοιτο!
exercises.answer: May it never be! / By no means! / God forbid!

exercises.question: What mood? τί ἂν θέλοι τοῦτο λέγειν;

readingPassage.greek: Εἴ τις ἔχοι σοφίαν, εὐδαίμων ἂν εἴη. Μὴ γένοιτο ἡμᾶς ἀπολέσθαι. Ὁ κύριος ὑμῖν δῴη εἰρήνην.
readingPassage.translation: If someone should have wisdom, he would be happy. May it not happen that we perish. May the Lord give you peace.
